page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache and instruction set support for AVX and AVX-512F. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a lean 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it connects via a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the average tier for general processing, scoring 1397.0 in Geekbench single-core and 5272.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 10428.01. Memory subsystem tests show 59.61 GB/sec read and 42.56 GB/sec write throughput on uncached 256 MB blocks, supporting high-rate in-memory tasks such as Redis SET operations at 7.86 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 9.4 GB/sec. However, machine learning inference displays significant hardware constraints: while a lightweight 135M model processes 737.38 prompt tokens per second, medium 7B parameter model execution yields weak performance at 15.97 prompt tokens and 7.76 generation tokens per second due to memory size and bandwidth limits.

The 1:1 memory-to-core ratio delivers compute density at an entry-level operational profile, avoiding unnecessary memory overhead for calculation-heavy tasks. Because persistent storage must be attached remotely via network block storage, persistent disk latency is decoupled from local instance lifecycles. The instance is suited for compute-focused worker nodes, build servers, lightweight microservices, static web delivery, and distributed batch processing pipelines that operate within an 8.0 GB working footprint.
